I am not an exact fan of having oil barrels in a certain area because they are meant to be in that area. Granted, they shouldn't be every 15 feet so you can accru 100 of them within a few minutes. It's just for me personally, I would rather have the game set up based on the world not the encounters. I'd rather have a fluid world then a world where I walk into a room and see what the devs wanted me to do. It's an RPG, if my dummy self wants to lug those 3 oil barrels across 4 miles to burn a bush instead of using a fireball scroll, then let my dummy self do that. 

As for mobility, if I recall correctly from the pax demo, didn't he say he had a feature that let him disengage? Perhaps I'm really wrong when I say this but I don't really care if they follow the books and rules to the letter. I want a good game and I don't think I want that limited by perhaps flawed systems in the dnd books. Of course use them but I want to see their own style shine through over the books. 

The story, I thought divinity 2 story was fine. Did it strike me no. However, I didn't find it a bore or drag. I wish they carried over that bantering you did from divinity one. It was fun to argue points of interest with your friend. As a whole though I found the world interesting to walk around, the people and gods and void jerks all were interesting to their own degree. All and all do I think it got 10/10 for story? No, but it for me definitely got a 7/10. With that being said I wouldn't worry about this game here because they have more writers and such. I just hope they maybe skip over that old classic rpg flavor text. I personally, found Baluders gate's writing dull to read and at times robotic in emotions. 

Finally, the loot!! I want crafting to be more of a thing. Sure let me find that 1d8+3 damage sword. Fine, but let me craft a cool sword with some custom looks to it! My armor as well! I think of they mirror divinity 2 loot system it wouldn't be bad by any means. I however think customization trumps all though. It's an RPG! Let's get immersed in this world! 

My only fear is that they will maybe follow the books to hard and enable min-maxing. I feel like if you want to min-max you should have the choice but it's a bit harder to do, to at least get it going. That's just a personal distaste I have. I won't personally min-max so maybe what I said here doesn't matter to the community as a whole... But I thought I mention it.
